geo.label: Fed: March lift-off signalled, balance-sheet runoff next
parts: Macro Stance

US growth looks strong in the rear-view mirror, and the Fed has stopped being patient. Fourth-quarter GDP grew at a 6.9% annualised pace, CNBC reported [[n1892]], and the Washington Post noted the 5.7% full-year gain was the fastest since 1984 [[n1906]]. Reuters credited fiscal stimulus for that performance [[n0151]], which is exactly why the impulse fades from here. Sentiment is already rolling over: Business Insider reported that Americans' economic hopes plummeted to decade lows in January as Omicron spread [[n1911]], and the White House is warning that the Omicron spike could skew the January jobs report [[n1934]]. We are Mixed: demand is intact, but the policy reaction function now dominates asset pricing.
Rates & Curve

The front end did the repricing. The 2Y closed at 1.18% and the 10Y at 1.79%, a 10Y–2Y spread of +61 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31). Over twenty observations the 2Y rose 45 bps from 0.73% while the 10Y rose 27 bps from 1.52%, flattening the spread by 18 bps: a bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more) that still leaves a moderately steep curve. In the last five observations the 2Y added 19 bps against only 4 bps for the 10Y, so the market is pricing hikes, not a higher growth trajectory. Standard Chartered expects the curve to flatten and possibly invert this year, Reuters reported [[n1993]], and a Reuters poll had already penciled in three hikes this year [[n1854]]. With the 3M bill at 0.22%, the 10Y–3M gap is still +157 bps, so the curve is not yet signalling recession.
New / Most Important

The Fed's January 25–26 meeting [[n1962]] pointed to a March hike, CNBC reported [[n1228]], with Reuters saying Powell vowed a sustained inflation fight [[n1227]]. Reuters' 'Mr. Nimble' framing captures the risk that the gradual script is gone [[n1967]], and the plan to shrink the balance sheet adds a second tightening channel [[n1225]]. Equities absorbed it badly before bouncing: Reuters said the Nasdaq narrowly missed its worst January ever as Wall Street gained on the final session [[n0094]]. The S&P 500 closed at 4,515.55 index points, +1.89% on the session but -5.26% over twenty sessions; the Nasdaq 100 rose +3.29% to 14,930.05 yet sits -8.52% over the same window; the VIX fell -10.23% to 24.83 index points, still +7.61 points above its level twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Playbook ✓

Action: keep a quality-over-duration tilt—own cash-generative megacaps, energy and banks, trim unprofitable growth into rebounds, and pair it with a 2s10s flattener. Trigger: add to the flattener while the 2Y keeps rising faster than the 10Y; keep trimming growth while the VIX stays well above its year-end level of 17.22 index points. What changes the call: a January payrolls report too weak to dismiss as Omicron noise, or a bear steepening in which the 10Y rises while the 2Y stalls, would argue for closing the flattener and re-adding duration-sensitive equities. DXY at 96.54 index points (-0.75% on the session) shows the dollar is no longer a one-way hedge (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).

geo.label: ECB on hold, BoE hiking, gas supply risk
parts: Macro Stance

Europe's problem is energy supply and policy asymmetry rather than demand. A Reuters poll had euro zone inflation running hotter while ECB rates stay on ice [[n1120]], and ING set out the ECB's trade-off between rate hikes and quantitative tightening [[n1142]]. With Russia–Ukraine tension feeding straight into gas prices, we are Bearish on the region's macro mix even though equities have held up relatively well.
Activity & Inflation

German inflation eased in January, TorFX noted [[n1201]], which gives the ECB cover to wait. The bigger variable is gas: the Economist asks how Europe would cope if Russia cut supply [[n1179]], and CNBC reports Europe assessing its options as fears mount [[n0677]]. Dutch TTF closed at 84.67 EUR/MWh, -8.03% on the session but +20.37% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), the profile of a market carrying a supply premium that swings with each diplomatic signal. Equities are pricing resilience, not stress: Euronews said European shares shrugged off the Fed with defensives leading [[n0480]].
New / Most Important

Qatar is seeking EU guarantees that emergency gas stays within the bloc, Reuters reported in an exclusive [[n1187]], and Washington says Nord Stream 2 won't happen if Russia invades, per DW [[n1159]]. The STOXX 600 closed at 468.88 index points (+0.72%, -4.31% over twenty sessions), a smaller drawdown than the S&P 500's -5.26%, and the DAX ended at 15,471.20 index points (+0.99%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). In the UK, sterling sat near a 23-month high against the euro as the Bank of England approached its decision [[n1241]].
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight gas-intensive cyclicals and keep European exposure in banks and energy majors. Trigger: hold while TTF stays above its year-end level of 70.34 EUR/MWh. What changes the call: verifiable de-escalation that pushes TTF back toward that reference, or an ECB signal that it will follow the Bank of England toward tightening, which would favour banks further and lift cyclicals.

geo.label: PBOC easing as the West tightens
parts: Macro Stance

China's cycle is out of phase with the West: as the Fed prepares to tighten, Bloomberg reports that China's central bank is seizing the moment for stimulus [[n0127]]. The starting point is weakening. Reuters said January factory activity growth slowed and demand waned as COVID surged [[n0177]], and an official had warned that factories face 'rather large' downward pressure in the first quarter, CNBC reported [[n0113]]. We are Mixed: policy is turning supportive and offshore equities have started to respond, but property and zero-COVID still cap the growth multiplier. With the Shanghai Composite's last completed session on 2022-01-28, the first onshore verdict on the easing is still pending.
PMIs & Activity

The official January PMIs describe deceleration rather than collapse. Reuters reported factory activity growth slowed [[n0177]], Hürriyet Daily News carried the line that factory activity edged down [[n0188]], and ABN AMRO argues the January PMIs indicate quarter-on-quarter growth will drop in the first quarter [[n0186]]. That follows 8.1% growth in 2021, the fastest in a decade, per Global Times [[n0104]], with fixed-asset investment up 4.9 pct for the year, per Macau Business [[n0106]]. Industrial profits rebounded in 2021 as production improved, China Daily reported [[n0162]], and total trade topped $6 trillion for the first time, according to Pandaily [[n0100]]. The mix matters: external demand carried 2021, and HSBC warns that disruptions in China can send 'ripple-effects' across the global supply chain, CNBC reported [[n0191]].
Credit Impulse

The policy signal is clear even if credit data still have to confirm it. The PBOC cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, CNBC reported [[n0110]], after trimming rates on medium-term loans and reverse repos, per Fibre2Fashion [[n0114]]; the BBC tied the cuts to slowing growth [[n0103]]. The transmission problem sits in bank balance sheets: Nikkei Asia reports that Minsheng, a major Evergrande creditor, faces a wave of bad loans [[n0132]], precisely the channel that blunts a rate cut. Our read is that the credit impulse turns up only if easing reaches developers and local governments; until then lower rates mainly compress yields and support duration rather than activity. A broadening of cuts beyond the policy corridor would be the confirmation signal.
Property

Property remains the binding constraint. The AFR reports Beijing is considering breaking up Evergrande to contain the crisis [[n0143]], The Real Deal says Oaktree seized an Evergrande property worth $1B [[n0154]], and Reuters chronicled the dashed dreams of Evergrande's showpiece resort island [[n0195]]. Bloomberg describes Chinese cities selling land to themselves as the crisis deepens [[n0133]], which props up local fiscal receipts on paper while masking weak private demand. Forbes counts a $30 billion drop in top property tycoons' fortunes, with more losses expected [[n0118]]. The one stabilising datapoint is that new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs, Business Recorder reported [[n0101]]. That is a price-cut-led stabilisation, not a volume recovery.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade friction is sticky rather than escalating. CNN explains why Biden is keeping Trump's China tariffs in place [[n0138]], the WTO said China can impose $645 million of retaliatory tariffs on US imports, per the Jersey Evening Post [[n0128]], and the EU escalated its trade dispute with Beijing over Lithuania, the BBC reported [[n0153]]. In technology, the SCMP warns that US–Japan restrictions on tech exports to China risk a 'major impact' [[n0122]], and Reuters reports Micron will shut DRAM chip design operations in Shanghai [[n0392]]. Domestically the policy mix is pro-growth but state-steered: CNBC notes another major Chinese tech firm expanding use of the country's digital currency [[n0140]], a reminder that payments remain state-directed.
Markets & Flows

Offshore Chinese equities closed the lunar year on a rebound. The Hang Seng ended at 23,802.26 index points, +1.07% on the session and +2.27% over twenty sessions, and Tencent rose +2.43% to 447.54 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31); the SCMP framed it as a January gain closing the Year of the Ox after a slump [[n0193]]. US-listed ADRs moved harder: KWEB jumped +9.74% to 37.41 USD and the Alibaba ADR +9.16% to 125.79 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Onshore, the Shanghai Composite's last session left it at 3,361.44 index points, -7.12% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28). The gap is regulatory as much as macro: CNBC argues the crackdown on Chinese IPOs in the US could make investors think twice about betting on tech [[n0131]].
New / Most Important

The newest signals are the January PMIs and the policy pivot. ABN AMRO's warning on first-quarter growth [[n0186]] lands as Bloomberg describes the PBOC using the Fed's tightening window to ease [[n0127]]. George Soros warned China is facing an economic crisis, CNN reported [[n0192]], a view the onshore index has partly discounted but the ADR bounce has not. The Winter Olympics backdrop limits any near-term reopening: the Guardian notes sport, politics and Covid colliding in Beijing [[n0179]], and Al Jazeera reports Hong Kong locking down homes in a COVID lesson taken from Beijing [[n0169]]. The signals conflict, but the direction of policy has changed.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold a modest overweight in offshore China internet (KWEB, Alibaba, Tencent) funded from onshore cyclicals, sized small. Trigger: add only if the reopening onshore session confirms the ADR move and the Shanghai Composite starts recovering toward its 3,619.19 index points reference; cut if the ADRs give back the session's gain. What changes the call: evidence that rate cuts are reaching developers, such as an Evergrande restructuring path that protects homebuyers, would justify rotating into onshore cyclicals; a fresh US delisting step would end the trade. ⚠ Divergence: offshore internet rallied as if easing were already working, while the official PMIs, Minsheng's bad loans and a -7.12% onshore index say transmission has not happened yet.

geo.label: BOJ on hold, debating hike messaging
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the one major economy where inflation arrives as a relief rather than a threat, but activity is wobbling. Reuters reported that factory output dipped more than expected as risks emerged [[n1404]], while a Reuters exclusive revealed the BOJ debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up [[n1379]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,001.98 index points, +1.07% on the session but -6.59% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). We are Mixed: corporate pricing power is improving, yet growth momentum and border restrictions argue against chasing the index.
Activity & Currency

The price signal is cultural as much as statistical: Reuters reported Japan's 'miracle' snack getting its first price hike in decades [[n1389]], and the Asahi warns surging prices could pinch consumers and derail recovery hopes [[n1400]]. December exports and imports hit record highs by value as bottlenecks eased [[n1381]], but imports also hit records on surging energy prices, per the Seattle Times [[n1382]], which worsens the terms of trade and tends to weigh on the yen through a larger energy bill. A Fed that is tightening while the BOJ only debates messaging keeps rate differentials working against the currency, which flatters exporters such as Toyota (2,245.50 JPY, +6.40% over twenty sessions) more than consumers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31); Reuters notes Toyota remains the world's biggest car seller, widening its lead on VW [[n0659]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer exporters and price-setters such as Toyota over high-multiple tech such as Tokyo Electron (-17.25% over twenty sessions) and SoftBank Group (-6.44%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Trigger: add if the BOJ's messaging debate turns into explicit guidance, which would reward pricing power and domestic financials. What changes the call: another industrial-output miss or a sharp yen rebound on global risk aversion would hit the exporter leg; then rotate toward domestic defensives.

geo.label: RBA pivot pressure after the CPI shock
parts: Macro Stance

Australia has moved from inflation laggard to inflation surprise. The AFR reported a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0015]] and argues inflation will force an RBA interest rate pivot [[n0018]], with economists predicting increases from mid-2022 [[n0027]]. A jobless rate at a 13-year low, per The Australian, removes the labour-market excuse [[n0010]]. We are Bearish on rate-sensitive Australia while the RBA ponders its next step, as the ABC put it [[n0058]].
Demand & Financing

Household balance sheets are the transmission channel. Domain reports Australia's median house price hit a record $1.066 million [[n0028]], News.com.au flags an 'ominous sign' for house prices [[n0049]], and Bloomberg described a bond meltdown haunting the central bank as inflation builds [[n0011]]. Banks are already trading the risk: Commonwealth Bank closed at 93.74 AUD, -2.02% on the session and -8.34% over twenty sessions, while the S&P/ASX 200 ended at 6,971.60 index points, -7.21%. Miners are the offset, with BHP +11.20% and Rio Tinto +12.08% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), as Reuters' Russell described iron ore rallying on Australian supply fears and China demand hopes [[n0033]].
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Australian banks and housing-linked names versus the miners. Trigger: maintain while CBA stays below its 102.27 AUD level of twenty sessions ago and pricing of RBA hikes keeps moving earlier. What changes the call: an RBA that leans against market pricing, as The Conversation argues is warranted [[n0042]], would ease pressure on the banks; a China-led iron ore reversal would undercut the miner leg.

geo.label: Rates rising, VAT shield from February
parts: Macro Stance

Poland closed 2021 with growth most of Europe would envy: GUS put 2021 GDP growth at 5.7%, Obserwator Gospodarczy reported [[n1592]], and Bankier called it a strong rebound for the Polish economy [[n1601]]. PKO BP economists, quoted by Parkiet, say the fundamentals are strong [[n1589]]. Yet Rzeczpospolita warned of a slowdown masked by statistics, with inflation and interest rates already curbing appetites [[n1618]]. Inflation ended 2021 at 8.6%, per 300Gospodarka [[n1436]], and Credit Agricole raised its inflation forecast for 2022 to 7.5% and for the following year to 5.5%, Bankier reported [[n1439]]. We are Mixed: nominal growth and bank earnings are strong, but real incomes, mortgage costs and a frontline security position keep the risk premium sticky.
Markets

Warsaw has been the cheap market few wanted to own. Strefa Inwestorów argues the GPW is priced really low because investors fear a crash and a crisis [[n1595]], and Parkiet described Monday's session as a rebound after declines [[n1607]]. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 38.07 PLN, +1.20% on the session but -2.61% over twenty sessions, while the dollar-based EPOL rose +1.43% to 20.53 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Leadership is concentrated in banks: Bank Pekao closed at 135.50 PLN (+11.07% over twenty sessions), mBank at 465.20 PLN (+9.41% over five) and PKO Bank Polski at 47.64 PLN (+6.03% over twenty) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The currency is the pressure valve: Money.pl reported the Ukraine conflict hitting the zloty [[n1451]], which tightens financial conditions at a moment when the central bank's leadership is itself contested.
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is pulling in two directions. The anti-inflation shield cuts VAT on food, energy and fuels from 1 February, Prawo.pl reported [[n1606]], and the government published the template and scope of the Tarcza Antyinflacyjna [[n1556]]; TVN24 even quoted analysts telling drivers to wait until Tuesday to refuel [[n1546]]. Credit Agricole argued, per Bankier, that the food-VAT cut will contribute to an increase in inflation [[n1432]]. Polski Ład remains politically toxic: Money.pl quotes critics calling the tax reform a 'monster' rather than a system of tax justice [[n1520]], and Rzeczpospolita tallies who gains or loses take-home pay [[n1578]]. Monetary governance is contested too: Rzeczpospolita reports that Adam Glapiński's candidacy for a second term as NBP president is poorly rated [[n1598]] and that PiS has a problem as the Sejm delays electing MPC (RPP) members [[n1519]]. Temporary tax cuts, a contested central-bank leadership and an MPC in transition argue for a higher term premium.
Corporate & Sectors

Energy and fuel names carry policy risk. Comparic noted PKN Orlen shares at their lowest in a month despite record oil prices [[n1505]]; Orlen closed at 71.00 PLN, -4.49% over twenty sessions, while utilities PGE (7.65 PLN, -5.11%) and Tauron (2.40 PLN, -9.42%) lag with heavy coal and gas cost exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Orlen is still positioning for the gas transition, with TVP 3 reporting interest in an LNG terminal in Police [[n1548]]. Coking-coal miner JSW is the momentum outlier, +14.97% over five sessions to 39.55 PLN, which Bankier described as an accelerating rebound [[n1474]]. Consumer names are bifurcated: Pepco is back at its IPO price, per Bankier [[n1511]], and -15.62% over twenty sessions at 39.25 PLN, while CD Projekt jumped +8.33% to 180.06 PLN on the day Spider's Web reported a new game in the Witcher world arriving this year [[n1602]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Strefa Inwestorów notes InPost has lost 64% of its valuation a year after its IPO [[n1508]].
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is NATO's frontline in the Russia–Ukraine standoff. TVN24 reported Russian airborne troops in Brest, at the Polish border and a few dozen kilometres from Ukraine [[n1497]], and Business Insider Polska showed satellite images of Russia's massive build-up on the Ukrainian border [[n1480]]. Warsaw has contingency plans to evacuate diplomats from Ukraine, a deputy foreign minister told TVN24 [[n1539]], and TVN24 relayed BBC reporting on a new alliance linking London, Kyiv and Warsaw [[n1581]]. Prime Minister Morawiecki said Poland must simply stand on the side of the attacked, Rzeczpospolita reported [[n1567]]. Energy is the second front: wnp.pl reports Gazprom wants a surcharge from PGNiG to set an example for other buyers [[n1481]], and the Warsaw Institute examines what Gazprom pays to transit gas through Belarus [[n1425]]. Polish firms told Money.pl they are prepared to react to the tension around Ukraine [[n1516]].
New / Most Important

The fresh information is the GDP release and the shield. GUS's 2021 GDP data, reported by Money.pl [[n1610]], arrived alongside GUS's 2021 wage figures [[n1621]], just as rising WIBOR feeds through to households: 300Gospodarka asks what happens to a mortgage if WIBOR rises by half [[n1573]], and Spider's Web tells zloty mortgage holders they will now feel like Swiss-franc borrowers, or worse [[n1452]]. Banks gain on margins, but the household squeeze is building, which is why Rzeczpospolita's slowdown warning matters more than the headline growth rate.
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight Polish banks (PKO Bank Polski, Bank Pekao, mBank) against an underweight in state utilities and fuel (PGE, Tauron, Orlen), keeping country exposure small via EPOL or the WIG20 tracker given security risk. Trigger: stay with it while Pekao holds above its 122.00 PLN level of twenty sessions ago and WIBOR keeps rising. What changes the call: an escalation through Belarus that sends the zloty sharply weaker would hit foreign-held bank shares first, so cut on such a move; making the VAT shield permanent would worsen the inflation outlook and the bond term premium. ⚠ Divergence: 5.7% growth [[n1592]] and rallying bank shares contrast with Rzeczpospolita's warning that rates and inflation are already curbing demand, and with a market that Strefa Inwestorów says is priced for a crash.
Narrative

Technology is splitting into cash compounders and duration trades. XLK closed at 161.97 USD, +2.51% on the session and +4.41% over five, but -6.84% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31); Barron's noted tech stocks had a historically bad January even after a two-day rally [[n1107]].
Reported

Apple's sales and profit topped estimates as the chip-shortage hit eased, Reuters reported [[n0450]], and the stock racked up its biggest one-day gain since July 2020 [[n0581]]. Microsoft beat on earnings and revenue and delivered an upbeat fiscal third-quarter forecast, per CNBC [[n0272]]. Intel's first-quarter forecast missed the Street, per the Fiji Times [[n1049]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is coming from pricing and mix rather than volume: Apple rose +8.14% over five sessions to 174.78 USD and Microsoft +4.93% to 310.98 USD, a premium for guidance visibility (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The Commerce Department says chip shortages will persist, Reuters reported [[n1716]], which caps hardware volumes but supports pricing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Higher yields are hurting unprofitable software far more than megacaps, so 'tech' as a bloc is the wrong unit. Owning Apple against a basket like ARKK, -20.26% over twenty sessions, expresses the rate view more cleanly than a blanket XLK underweight (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Narrative

Communication services is where January's narrative damage concentrated. XLC closed at 73.95 USD, +2.27% on the session and -4.80% over twenty sessions; Netflix is -29.10% over twenty sessions at 427.14 USD despite +11.13% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Verizon beat quarterly subscriber-addition estimates and expects a strong 2022, Reuters reported [[n0309]], and AT&T is readying a revamped firm after selling its media unit [[n0330]]. Spotify's content risk became a price event: TheWrap said it lost $2 billion of value after Neil Young's protest over Joe Rogan [[n0704]], before the stock rebounded on Rogan's apology, per The Week [[n0831]].
EPS Upside Watch

Meta Platforms (FB), at 313.26 USD and -6.86% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), is the test of metaverse spending: Business Insider cites analyst estimates that the effort already generates close to $3 billion a year in revenue [[n1044]], while the WSJ reports the company's cryptocurrency venture is winding down and selling assets [[n0364]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Insider buying is not a bottom signal on its own. Co-CEO Reed Hastings bought $20 million of Netflix shares after the drop, Bloomberg reported [[n0634]], but subscriber growth, not insider sponsorship, sets the multiple.
Narrative

Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of the front-end repricing. XLF closed at 39.06 USD, +0.03% over twenty sessions while the S&P 500 fell -5.26%; Wells Fargo is +12.13% and Citigroup +7.83% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Bank of America's fourth-quarter profits topped analysts' projections with revenue up 10%, per The Business Journals [[n0955]]; Blackstone reported record fourth-quarter earnings, Reuters said [[n0456]]; and Nasdaq's profit topped Street views on an IPO surge [[n1012]]. Visa, Mastercard and American Express posted 'monster' revenue updates, per Payments Industry Intelligence [[n0671]].
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income is the upside lever after the 2Y rose 45 bps in twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31). Compensation is the offset: Bank of America is raising base pay for top bankers, Reuters reported [[n0339]], and Goldman Sachs lifted CEO David Solomon's pay to $35 million [[n0610]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Capital-markets revenue, not credit, is the weak link: WeTransfer's owner cancelled its IPO citing market volatility, Reuters reported [[n1236]]. Prefer deposit-rich lenders such as Bank of America (+3.71% over twenty sessions) and the regional-bank KRE (+1.06%) over advisory-heavy Goldman Sachs (-7.29%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Narrative

Energy is the market's inflation hedge with earnings attached. XLE closed at 65.92 USD, +18.77% over twenty sessions, as Brent settled at 91.21 USD/bbl (+17.27%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Reuters reported oil posted its biggest monthly gain in a year on tight supply and political tensions [[n1798]].
Reported

Chevron kicked off the oil industry's fourth-quarter results with a miss, Reuters reported [[n0595]], yet the New York Times called it the company's best quarter since 2014 [[n1076]] and Bloomberg said the stock hit a record after a surprise dividend boost [[n0463]]. Halliburton doubled quarterly profit and raised its dividend [[n0970]].
EPS Upside Watch

Oilfield services carry the operating leverage: Schlumberger is +30.45% and Occidental +29.94% over twenty sessions versus Exxon Mobil's +24.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), and Oil & Gas 360 reports Halliburton seeing frac equipment orders double [[n0978]]. Henry Hub gas at 4.87 USD/MMBtu, +30.67% over twenty sessions, adds upside for gas-weighted producers.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The risk is supply, not demand: the EIA forecasts OPEC production will grow in 2022 despite Libyan outages [[n0081]], and a revived Iran deal, which the New York Times says the US and allies are close to [[n1366]], would add barrels. The market rewards capital discipline over volume growth.
Narrative

Industrials have demand but not margins. XLI closed at 100.74 USD, -4.79% over twenty sessions, and Caterpillar is -5.96% over five sessions at 201.56 USD despite strong sales (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Caterpillar's sales soared but it warned of margin pressure, Reuters reported [[n0593]]. GE's shares fell as supply-chain woes hit fourth-quarter revenue [[n0245]]; 3M's profit beat on Omicron-driven N95 demand [[n0204]], but it was hit with a $110 million verdict in the latest military earplug trial [[n0571]]. Boeing posted a third annual loss in a row as Dreamliner costs hit $5.5 billion, per CNBC [[n0346]].
EPS Upside Watch

Aerospace orders are the upside: Boeing won a Qatar Airways order for 737 Max planes and new 777X freighters, CNBC reported [[n0770]], and Boeing rose +5.07% to 200.24 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Reuters says analysts are watching UPS automation efforts to offset increased wage costs [[n0761]], the swing factor for parcel margins.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Defence primes are the industrial hedge nobody needs until they do: Lockheed Martin is +9.49% over twenty sessions at 389.13 USD while ITA is -1.61% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The gap says investors are paying for geopolitical optionality in the primes, not for commercial aerospace.
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is where higher rates meet margin squeeze. XLY closed at 184.95 USD, -9.53% over twenty sessions, with Amazon -10.28% at 2,991.47 USD and Home Depot -11.57% at 366.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Tesla reported record yearly profit but warned that supply problems persist, the New York Times reported [[n1028]], and CBS said it won't roll out new models in 2022 because of chip shortages [[n0544]]. McDonald's profit was hit by rising costs and pandemic curbs, Reuters reported [[n0503]].
EPS Upside Watch

General Motors' $7 billion Michigan EV investment, per the company [[n0246]], and Reuters' view that Ford and GM are juggling today's challenges with tomorrow's promises [[n0607]] frame the autos debate: GM closed at 52.73 USD, -10.06% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Starbucks faces labour pressure as workers petition to unionise at 50 US stores, per Al Jazeera [[n0833]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla's +10.68% session to 936.72 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31) looks like short-covering rather than earnings upgrades. Elon Musk saying a robot matters more than new car models this year, per CNBC [[n1728]], lengthens the duration of the story at the worst moment for duration.
Narrative

Staples are proving pricing power but not immunity. XLP closed at 75.97 USD, -1.48% over twenty sessions, well ahead of the S&P 500; Coca-Cola is +3.04% over the same window while Costco is -11.02% at 505.13 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Diageo's sales jumped on premium spirits and bar restocking, Reuters reported [[n0474]], and the WSJ noted it is running low on spirits that take years to make [[n0477]]. France's Casino slumped after a profit warning, Reuters reported [[n1102]].
EPS Upside Watch

Price increases are flowing through: CNN reported Oscar Mayer hot dogs and Velveeta cheese will get more expensive [[n0365]], and Coca-Cola is teaming up with Molson Coors on Simply-branded alcoholic drinks [[n0231]]. Procter & Gamble at 160.45 USD and PepsiCo at 173.52 USD are flat to lower over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), so price-led beats are not fully priced.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Defensive does not mean cheap: Nestle is -7.85% over twenty sessions at 119.08 CHF (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), a reminder that long-duration staples de-rate with yields. The better staples bet is cost pass-through and supply security, illustrated by Walmart's investment in vertical-farming start-up Plenty, per CNBC [[n1639]].
Narrative

Health care is a stock-picker's sector with policy noise. XLV closed at 131.23 USD, -6.86% over twenty sessions; Moderna is -33.33% at 169.33 USD while Merck is +6.32% at 81.48 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Johnson & Johnson reported its fourth-quarter and full-year results [[n0983]], with ET HealthWorld noting prescription drugs and medical devices boosted the quarter [[n1018]]. Abbott weathered the COVID-testing swings with $7.7B in annual diagnostic sales, per Fierce Biotech [[n0999]], and UnitedHealth Group reported its fourth quarter [[n0958]].
EPS Upside Watch

Regulatory catalysts cut both ways: the US granted full approval to Moderna's COVID vaccine in adults, Reuters reported [[n0846]], while a Reuters insight says Merck's COVID pill is the last choice for US patients [[n0800]]. Eli Lilly warned the FDA could deny expanded use of its arthritis drug for eczema [[n0604]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The overlooked driver is pricing politics: STAT reports insulin makers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk boosted lobbying as Democrats eyed pricing reform [[n1680]], so the defensive bid in pharma comes with a legislative tail. Novo Nordisk is -7.92% over twenty sessions at 656.10 DKK (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Narrative

Materials are splitting between supply-constrained inputs and growth-sensitive metals. XLB closed at 84.45 USD, -6.80% over twenty sessions, but aluminum is +11.83% at 3,078.25 USD/t and palladium +23.12% at 2,349.20 USD/oz, while copper slipped -3.08% to 4.32 USD/lb (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported
Freeport-McMoRan's CEO says copper demand will continue to boom, CNBC reported [[n0467]], and U.S. Steel set a new stock buyback after the metal-price surge, per Bloomberg [[n0662]].
EPS Upside Watch

Fertiliser is the cleanest upside: Nutrien eyes a potash production boost amid turmoil in Russia and Belarus, Reuters reported [[n0774]], and the Investing News Network says supply disruptions pushed potash prices to a 13-year high [[n1689]]. Nutrien closed at 69.80 USD, still -7.18% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), so the earnings upside is not yet in the price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Gold is the laggard hedge: at 1,795.00 USD/oz, -1.84% over twenty sessions, it is not responding to geopolitics because real-rate repricing dominates; Livemint said gold failed to hold a breakout [[n1986]]. Miners such as Newmont (-1.37%) carry that drag (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), so prefer supply-constrained inputs over precious metals.
Narrative

Real estate is the purest duration casualty. XLRE closed at 47.34 USD, -8.63% over twenty sessions, worse than the S&P 500's -5.26%, as the 10Y rose 27 bps to 1.79% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31; US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Barron's reported Toll Brothers was double-downgraded on rising rates even as KB Home remains a top homebuilder pick [[n0492]], and Fortune said US home price growth decelerated again, with forecast models suggesting the peak rate is behind us [[n1913]].
EPS Upside Watch

Cash flows hold up better than prices because leases reprice with inflation over time, but Bloomberg warns that mortgage bond weakness threatens the US corporate debt market [[n1982]], which would raise refinancing costs. Opendoor at 9.93 USD, -32.03% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), shows how fast housing-linked multiples compress.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Convention says real estate hedges inflation; in a front-end-led hiking cycle it trades like a long bond. Leveraged property is where the cycle bites first, as Bloomberg's report of Chinese cities selling land to themselves shows [[n0133]], so the better real-asset exposure is pricing power in energy and materials.
Narrative

Utilities are caught between bond-proxy de-rating and fuel-cost politics. XLU closed at 69.25 USD, +1.90% on the session and -3.26% over twenty sessions; NextEra Energy is -16.32% at 78.12 USD while Duke Energy is +0.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

NextEra Energy named John Ketchum president and CEO, with Jim Robo becoming executive chairman, per PR Newswire [[n0281]]; Utility Dive framed Robo's retirement as following the company's 'strong' 2021 [[n0280]].
EPS Upside Watch

Regulated rate bases grow with capex: Georgia Power's plan confirms a move from coal to renewables, FOX 5 Atlanta reported [[n0790]]. But fuel pass-through is turning political: KRCR says PG&E customers are seeing higher utility bills on natural gas prices [[n1800]], and Duke Energy Florida customers face minimum $30 bills, per WFLA [[n0603]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Henry Hub at 4.87 USD/MMBtu (+30.67% over twenty sessions) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31) turns gas-heavy utilities into inflation losers rather than safe havens. Treat the sector as two groups: regulated renewable builders, where allowed returns rise with investment, and gas-dependent distributors, where bill politics cap recovery.
Narrative

European autos are pricing supply normalisation and EV capex at once. The STOXX Europe autos tracker closed at 60.85 EUR, +1.98% over five sessions but -2.01% over twenty; Renault is +11.14% at 34.92 EUR while Volkswagen's preference shares are +1.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

Daimler rebrands as Mercedes-Benz on Feb. 1, Reuters reported [[n0599]]; Mercedes-Benz Group closed at 69.93 EUR, +1.79% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Toyota remained the world's biggest car seller and widened its lead on Volkswagen, CNBC reported [[n0660]], and ACEA data show EU commercial vehicle registrations +9.6% in 2021 but -8.4% in December [[n1700]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen and Bosch teaming up on automated-driving software, per Reuters [[n0311]], and Bentley's $3.4 billion plan to offer only EVs by 2030, per CNBC [[n1698]], are long-dated; near-term earnings upside comes from pricing while chip supply stays tight.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Russia and China exposure is underappreciated: Stellantis plans to start exporting Russia-made minivans to Western Europe, Reuters reported [[n0293]], and China's GAC scolded Stellantis over its joint-venture plan [[n0464]]. The cheap-looking autos carry geopolitical supply-chain risk that a sanctions scenario could crystallise, so stay selective.
Narrative

Semiconductors rebounded hard on the last session but remain the epicentre of the duration sell-off. SOXX closed at 479.47 USD, +5.37% on the session and -11.59% over twenty; ASML's US line is -14.94% at 677.20 USD while TSMC's ADR is +1.93% at 122.63 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Reported

ASML's stock jumped as its earnings beat expectations, Barron's reported [[n0954]]; SK Hynix sees supply-chain issues improving in the second half with more chip demand, per Reuters [[n0535]]. Lam Research flagged fresh supply-chain issues that cast a pall over chip equipment, MarketWatch said [[n0499]], and Teradyne's great earnings were crushed on guidance, per Barron's [[n0543]].
EPS Upside Watch

STMicro will double investment to meet high chip demand, Reuters reported [[n0536]], and the WSJ notes TSMC overtook Chinese tech giants to become Asia's most valuable stock [[n0296]]. SK Hynix's +6.17% to 120,500.00 KRW (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28) shows memory being re-rated as supply visibility improves.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Leverage amplifies everything: SOXL rose +16.06% on the session but is -34.45% over twenty (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Reuters reports Nvidia preparing to walk away from its Arm acquisition [[n1687]], removing an overhang but also a growth option; Nvidia's +7.21% bounce is positioning, not a fundamental reset.

earnings_pattern.title: Beats are bought only when guidance and margins hold
parts: Rewarded

The market rewarded beats that came with pricing power and capital returns. Apple beat estimates with all-time record revenue, the Guardian reported [[n1074]], and rose +8.14% over five sessions to 174.78 USD; Visa (+12.05%) and Mastercard (+10.58%) rallied over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31) after the payment networks' revenue updates. Microsoft's stock fell 5% after hours on its beat, GeekWire reported [[n0067]], yet finished +4.93% over five sessions once the upbeat forecast was digested. Chevron touched a record high ahead of its results, Reuters noted [[n0352]], showing how much payout visibility is worth.
Punished

Misses on guidance or margins were punished regardless of the headline beat. Intel can't grow profits even during a global chip shortage, The Conversation argued [[n1084]], and it closed -6.01% over five sessions at 48.82 USD. Robinhood posted a $423 million net loss and its shares sank after hours, Reuters reported [[n0529]], while Caterpillar fell -5.96% over five sessions despite soaring sales (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). In Europe, Siemens Gamesa reported a big first-quarter loss and cut guidance, Wind Power Monthly said [[n0964]], and Saipem issued a profit warning as margins deteriorated [[n1106]].
Pattern

The common thread is margin, not demand. Supply-chain costs at GE, Caterpillar and Lam Research, labour and commodity costs at McDonald's, as Bloomberg described [[n0504]], and forward guidance now outrank revenue beats. With the 2Y up 45 bps over twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31), the discount rate punishes any company that pushes profits further out, which is why Tesla's decision to skip new models this year mattered as much as its record profit.
Attention into EPS

Attention is concentrating where January's drawdowns were deepest—Netflix (-29.10% over twenty sessions), AMD (-20.60%) and Coinbase (-24.65%)—so the next prints there carry asymmetric reactions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Fortune's look at why Wall Street thinks the metaverse will be worth trillions [[n0562]] shows how much optionality is still embedded in platform valuations.
Playbook

Buy beats only where guidance is raised or margins are defended (Apple, payment networks, energy majors) and fade beats that come with cautious outlooks, especially equipment and industrial names flagging supply costs. Trigger: a stock that holds its post-earnings gap for three sessions. What changes the call: a decline in the 2Y that revives duration appetite would make guidance cuts in growth names forgivable again.

underowned.title: Grain and fertiliser: the Ukraine supply chain that equities ignore
parts: Attention Gap

Equity attention on Russia–Ukraine centres on gas and defence, but Reuters notes Ukraine's rising role in grain exports complicates the crisis's impact [[n1699]], and an analyst told Successful Farming that grain exports would likely be disrupted in a conflict [[n1789]]. Yet CBOT wheat closed at 761.25 US cents/bu, -1.23% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Exposure & Risk

Soybeans hit $15 per bushel, per Successful Farming [[n1805]], and closed at 1,490.50 US cents/bu, +12.17% over twenty sessions; corn is +5.52% at 626.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Fertiliser producers such as Nutrien, CF Industries (-2.70%) and Mosaic (+1.68%) carry the input side. The risk is a diplomatic settlement that removes the premium quickly.
Trigger to Watch

Any disruption to Ukrainian grain shipments, or a sanctions step touching Belarusian potash; Nutrien's push to boost potash output amid the Russia and Belarus turmoil [[n0774]] shows supply security is becoming a pricing factor.

underowned.title: Atlantic LNG: Europe's swing supply
parts: Attention Gap

Qatar wants EU guarantees that emergency cargoes stay in Europe [[n1187]], a Reuters explainer asks whether Qatari gas can offset Russian disruption [[n1190]], and the ABC explains why Australia is offering LNG to Europe [[n1416]]. The physical-flow story is clear; the listed exposure to it is not crowded.
Exposure & Risk

Henry Hub closed at 4.87 USD/MMBtu, +21.03% over five sessions, after Reuters explained a record 70% one-day spike [[n1758]]; Shell, now trading under a simpler single-line share structure [[n0824]], is +16.33% over twenty sessions at 1,886.60 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). US gas volatility cuts both ways for buyers of the theme.
Trigger to Watch

TotalEnergies aims to restart its $20 billion Mozambique LNG project in 2022, Reuters reported [[n0844]]; a firm restart decision or EU-level supply guarantees would extend the bid for LNG-linked equities.

underowned.title: Defence primes and European rearmament
parts: Attention Gap

Defence has drawn less attention than energy despite the Russian build-up. Lockheed Martin posted better-than-expected profit and reiterated its 2022 sales outlook [[n0266]], General Dynamics beat profit forecasts on higher aerospace sales [[n0371]], and Raytheon Technologies' sales forecast disappointed [[n0288]].
Exposure & Risk

Lockheed Martin is +9.49% over twenty sessions at 389.13 USD and Rheinmetall +8.51% at 92.10 EUR, but Northrop Grumman is -4.44% and ITA -1.61% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risks: the FTC suing to block Lockheed's $4.4 billion Aerojet deal, per Reuters [[n0302]], and any de-escalation.
Trigger to Watch

European budget signals. Germany's offer of 5,000 helmets to Ukraine was met with disdain, CNBC reported [[n1296]], so any shift in Berlin's defence stance would be a material re-rating trigger for European defence names.

underowned.title: Japan's pricing-power pivot
parts: Attention Gap

Global investors still treat Japan as a deflation market, but Reuters reports a decades-old 'miracle' snack getting its first price hike [[n1389]] and the BOJ debating how to message an eventual rate hike [[n1379]]. Breadth matters more than any single print.
Exposure & Risk

Toyota at 2,245.50 JPY is +6.40% over twenty sessions while the Nikkei 225 is -6.59% and EWJ -4.30% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The Asahi reports the average Tokyo-area condo price at 62.6 million yen [[n0998]], a wealth effect behind domestic demand. The risk is weak output, after factory production dipped more than expected [[n1404]].
Trigger to Watch

Explicit BOJ guidance or a broadening of corporate price increases; the Guardian's report of Japan's favourite snack falling victim to global inflation [[n1399]] is the kind of breadth signal to track.

crypto.title: Bitcoin stabilises, but the crypto winter is not over
parts: Market Context

Crypto is trading as the highest-beta expression of the Fed repricing. Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 38,483.12 USD, +1.49% on the day and +4.43% over five days but -9.95% versus 42,735.86 USD on 2022-01-11; Ether closed at 2,688.28 USD (-16.98% over the same window) and Solana at 99.74 USD (-28.85%) (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-01-31). CNBC said investors fear a 'crypto winter' with bitcoin down 50% from record highs [[n0868]], and USA Today tied the slide to uncertainty in traditional markets and Fed concerns [[n0913]]. Listed proxies amplify the moves: Coinbase is -24.65% and MicroStrategy -32.41% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
New / Most Important

Private capital is still flowing to the industry's leaders: FTX raised $400 million at a $32 billion valuation, CNBC reported [[n0940]], with Bloomberg noting an eye to M&A [[n0945]]. Payments adoption continues, with Visa saying crypto-linked card usage hit $2.5 billion in its first quarter [[n0670]]. The counter-signal is fragility: Bloomberg reported hackers seized $80 million from Qubit in the latest DeFi attack [[n0918]], the IMF urged El Salvador to remove bitcoin as legal tender [[n0886]], and Paul Krugman sees 'disturbing' parallels with the subprime mortgage meltdown [[n0921]]. The sale of the Diem Group's assets to Silvergate [[n0822]] removes a big-tech stablecoin rival.
Playbook

Stance Mixed. Action: keep crypto exposure underweight and prefer bitcoin over higher-beta altcoins and miners. Trigger: add only on a daily close back above the 42,735.86 USD reference, which would show the Fed shock has been absorbed; until then, rebounds such as Iris Energy's +19.73% session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31) look like short-covering. What changes the call: a renewed rise in the 2Y or another large DeFi exploit would argue for cutting further, while stable yields and continued institutional fundraising would support a gradual rebuild.

flows.title: Liquidity is leaving the most speculative assets first
parts: Global Liquidity

The marginal dollar is getting more expensive. Beyond a March hike, the Fed is planning to cut its balance sheet, Reuters explained [[n1225]], and the Fiji Times summarised the Fed flagging a hike 'soon' alongside significant balance-sheet reduction [[n1231]]. The Economist argues quantitative tightening is no substitute for higher interest rates [[n1244]], implying hikes do the heavy lifting while runoff adds a slower drain. The Bank of England is sounding the QT klaxon with its second rate rise, a Reuters commentary said [[n1166]], and ING published a guide to its approach [[n1200]]. China is the counter-flow, cutting rates as growth slows [[n0103]], which is why offshore China and the dollar bloc are trading on different liquidity regimes. The Richmond Fed's study of why overnight reverse-repo usage rose [[n1936]] is a reminder that excess cash still sits in the system, cushioning the first stage of runoff.
Rates & Dollar

The Treasury curve is the transmission belt. With the 2Y at 1.18% and the 10Y at 1.79%, the 10Y–2Y spread sits at +61 bps after flattening 18 bps over twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31). Treasury ETFs show the duration loss: TLT is -3.91% and IEF -2.11% over twenty sessions, while SHY is only -0.69% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The dollar has been the release valve: Investing.com reported its biggest weekly rise in seven months on rate bets [[n1394]], before Reuters said the rally paused and may have seen a short-term peak [[n0063]]. DXY stands at 96.54 index points, +0.91% over twenty sessions. Al Jazeera notes emerging markets dreading a repeat of past Fed-hike shocks [[n1217]], and the EMB bond ETF is -3.37% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Credit Check

Credit is softening at the edges, not breaking. HYG closed at 84.70 USD, -2.65% over twenty sessions, and LQD at 127.76 USD, -3.59%, so investment grade has lost more than high yield because duration, not default risk, is driving prices (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Bloomberg warns that mortgage bond weakness threatens the US corporate debt market [[n1982]], the spread-contagion channel to watch. Risk appetite has not vanished: Bloomberg reported a leveraged-buyout boom built on an $18 billion bet in debt markets [[n1216]], and cat bond issuance hit a record $12.5 billion, per Bermuda Re [[n1213]]. In China, Minsheng's wave of bad loans [[n0132]] is the bank-credit stress point that could leak into Asian high yield.
Equity & Fund Flows

The retail bid has flipped: retail investors dumped stocks at Monday's open, MarketWatch reported from a JPMorgan analysis [[n0301]], and Barron's said meme-stock mania is on life support a year on [[n0574]]. Issuance is stalling: Reuters reported WeTransfer's owner cancelled its IPO citing volatility [[n1236]], and Global Finance says IPOs delivered their worst returns in a decade [[n1243]]. Concentrated buyers are stepping in selectively: Barron's said Pershing Square bought $1 billion of Netflix shares [[n0512]], and Bloomberg reported Paul Marshall's hedge fund made a historic move on value stocks [[n1224]]. Supply also comes from large holders: MacKenzie Scott sold $8.5B of Amazon stock, the New York Post reported [[n0802]]. Private markets are still raising money even as public issuance stalls: Blackstone teed up $11 billion in fresh capital for Asia deals, Bloomberg reported [[n0726]]. Abroad, Valor International reports a strong inflow of foreigners into Brazil's stock market [[n1212]], consistent with value-heavy emerging markets absorbing reallocation.
Portfolio Implication

Position for tighter liquidity without assuming a crash. Keep the quality tilt—energy, banks, cash-rich megacaps—and hold duration short through a 2s10s flattener until the 2Y stops outpacing the 10Y. Fund it from long-duration growth, unprofitable tech and crypto proxies, where retail selling and IPO withdrawals show the marginal buyer has stepped back. What changes the call: a stabilising 2Y together with HYG recovering toward its 87.01 USD year-end level would signal that liquidity stress is fading and justify re-adding beta.

anticipatory.title: January payrolls and the March lift-off
parts: What Is Priced

A March hike is priced: Reuters says the Fed is likely to move in March as Powell vows a sustained inflation fight [[n1227]], and the 2Y at 1.18% has risen 45 bps in twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-01-31). What is not priced is a payroll miss that the Fed could not explain away; the White House is already warning that the Omicron spike could skew the January jobs report [[n1934]].
Conditional Expression

If payrolls are weak but clearly Omicron-distorted, the front end should hold its gains: keep the flattener and own banks over long-duration tech. If payrolls are strong and wage growth keeps running hot—Time reported a record increase in US wage growth [[n1909]]—add to the 2s10s flattener and stay short duration-heavy indices such as the Nasdaq 100, -8.52% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Risk

A genuinely weak labour market would revive talk of a slower hiking path and squeeze the flattener, so size positions to tolerate a partial reversal of the 18 bps flattening rather than betting on a straight line.

anticipatory.title: Russia–Ukraine: escalation versus diplomacy
parts: What Is Priced

The US demanded at the UN that Russia explain its troop build-up, VOA reported [[n1355]], and CNBC cites analysts warning Russia is willing to go to war and incur sanctions [[n1363]]. Markets price a premium in energy—Brent at 91.21 USD/bbl, +17.27% over twenty sessions—but much less in broad European equities, with the STOXX 600 only -4.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31).
Conditional Expression

On escalation, own energy, defence primes and gas exposure, and underweight European autos and banks. On de-escalation, Kyiv's call for Russia to pull troops back from the border, per the Guardian [[n1344]], is the template: fade the energy premium and buy European cyclicals. Boeing's warning that the tensions are creating an 'adverse climate' for business [[n0769]] shows how far the damage could spread beyond Europe.
Risk

Sanctions design matters: the New York Times says US sanctions aimed at Russia could take a wide toll [[n1337]], and Bloomberg explains why a SWIFT ban is such a potent sanction [[n1294]]. Second-round effects could hit European banks harder than energy gains help.

anticipatory.title: Iran deal and oil's risk premium
parts: What Is Priced

Oil posted its biggest monthly gain in a year, Reuters said [[n1798]], with WTI at 88.15 USD/bbl, +17.21% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Yet the New York Times reports the US and allies are close to reviving the nuclear deal with Iran [[n1366]], and an official told NBC4 Washington there are just a 'handful of weeks' left to strike it [[n1358]].
Conditional Expression

A deal would add supply into a market whose shock absorbers Reuters describes as wearing thin [[n1710]]; express it by trimming high-beta producers such as Occidental (+29.94% over twenty sessions) while keeping integrated majors with dividend support (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). No deal, layered on Ukraine risk, keeps the premium intact.
Risk

The EIA forecasts OPEC production will grow despite Libyan outages [[n0081]], so supply could loosen even without Iran; in the other direction, Kpler maps the global trade and tanker risks of sanctions on Russian oil exports [[n1307]], a channel that could tighten markets abruptly.

anticipatory.title: Bank of England and RBA: the hawkish pivot test
parts: What Is Priced

A Reuters poll expects the Bank of England to raise rates again in February as inflation surges [[n1131]], and sterling sits near a 23-month high against the euro [[n1241]]. In Australia, the AFR argues inflation will force an RBA interest-rate pivot [[n0018]] while the ABC describes the RBA pondering its next step [[n0058]].
Conditional Expression

If the Bank of England hikes and sets out QT, favour UK banks such as HSBC (+17.60% over twenty sessions, 527.60 GBp) over gilts (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). If the RBA moves its guidance earlier, extend the underweight in Australian banks versus miners; if it resists, as the Vital Signs column carried by UNSW Sydney argued it should [[n0047]], cover part of that underweight.
Risk

Both banks face the same trap of tightening into a supply shock. The Economist says the Bank of England is determined to prevent a wage-price spiral [[n1160]], so a hawkish surprise could hit UK domestic cyclicals, while in Australia a hike debate would land on record house prices.

catalysts.title: Apple (AAPL) — record quarter, quality anchor
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Apple posted the largest revenue and profit in its history on the iPhone 13 despite parts shortages, CNET reported [[n0451]], and Yahoo Finance notes it is Morgan Stanley's top pick for 2022 [[n0764]]. The thesis: pricing power plus easing supply make Apple the quality anchor of a rate-shocked market.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 174.78 USD, +8.14% over five sessions but still -1.57% versus 177.57 USD twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risks: supply constraints re-tighten, or the multiple compresses further if the 10Y keeps climbing.
Trade Expression
Buy pullbacks while the post-earnings gain holds; the first target is a reclaim of 177.57 USD. Cut if the five-session gain is fully reversed, which would mean the beat is being sold.

catalysts.title: Chevron (CVX) — payout leader of the majors
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Chevron delivered its best quarter since 2014, the New York Times reported [[n1076]], and Bloomberg said a surprise dividend boost sent the stock to a record [[n0463]]. The thesis: capital returns at high oil prices make Chevron the lower-beta way to own the energy trade.
Price Hurdle & Risk

CVX closed at 131.33 USD, +11.91% over twenty sessions, lagging Exxon Mobil's +24.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risks: the quarter itself missed estimates, Reuters noted [[n0595]], and an Iran deal would cap crude.
Trade Expression

Own CVX against XLE as a lower-volatility energy expression and add on dips while Brent holds its twenty-session gain; exit if a confirmed Iran deal pushes Brent back toward its 77.78 USD/bbl year-end level.

catalysts.title: Sony Group (6758.T) — Bungie buys content depth
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Sony agreed to buy Destiny maker Bungie in a $3.6 billion deal, Barron's reported [[n0827]], and Business Insider said its shares jumped on the announcement as video-game M&A heats up [[n0828]]. The thesis: owned content for PlayStation as rivals consolidate.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The Tokyo line closed at 12,720.00 JPY, +3.96% on the session but -12.76% versus 14,580.00 JPY twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risks: integration costs and paying a premium in a market that punishes long-dated growth.
Trade Expression
Accumulate gradually below the 14,580.00 JPY reference while the Nikkei 225 stabilises; the trade is wrong if Sony keeps underperforming the index after the deal premium is priced.

catalysts.title: Netflix (NFLX) — sponsorship after the reset
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Pershing Square took a new position, Reuters reported [[n0331]], buying 3.1 million shares during the sell-off, per CNBC [[n0455]], and Reed Hastings bought $20M of stock on the dip, Deadline reported [[n0700]]. The thesis: activist and insider sponsorship after a growth reset.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NFLX closed at 427.14 USD, +11.13% on the session and +10.33% over five, but -29.10% versus 602.44 USD twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risk: subscriber growth disappoints again, and sponsorship does not change subscriber economics.
Trade Expression
Hold a half position rather than chasing the squeeze; add only if the rebound holds, and cut on a close that erases the +10.33% five-session bounce.

catalysts.title: Boeing (BA) — orders versus geopolitics
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Boeing struck a deal with Qatar Airways for 777-8 freighters and 737 Max 10 orders, Fox Business reported [[n0771]], with Simple Flying saying Qatar signed for up to 100 777X freighters and 737 MAXs [[n1783]]. But Boeing says Ukraine tensions are creating an 'adverse climate' for business, Reuters reported [[n0769]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

BA closed at 200.24 USD, +5.07% on the session and -0.54% versus 201.32 USD twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Risk: a third straight annual loss with Dreamliner costs hitting $5.5 billion, per CNBC [[n0346]].
Trade Expression
Buy a close above 201.32 USD, but keep it small because a Ukraine-Russia conflict could derail global aerospace, as The Air Current explains [[n1692]].

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC) — margins under pressure
parts: Catalyst & Thesis
